Gold is entering a historically favorable period of the year:

Gold prices have gained +1.5% in July on average over the last 20 years, making it the 2nd-strongest month of the year.

Gold prices have also recorded positive returns in 65% of July months, the 2nd-best win rate of any month.

The strongest July over this period was in 2020, when gold returned +10.7%.

The only better month historically has been August, with an average gain of +1.6% since 2005.

August also posted a 55% win rate, with its strongest year coming in 2011, when gold returned +12.1%.

By comparison, June has historically been the weakest month, with an average decline of -0.4% and just 40% positive readings since 2005.

Seasonality is turning in favor of gold bulls.

I've mostly avoided any involvement in the BIP-110 debate, but the language/sentiment data I've explored is too interesting not to share.

One of the sentiment metrics I watch closely is "conviction".

This is basically measuring the amount of confidence in someone's language over time (gold line).

The inverse of this is hedging (blue line), which shows up when people are less confident or put more qualifiers around how they speak.

In the chart below, you can visualize the language data for these most active BIP-110 supporters I've tracked over the last four years. 

Their confidence has fallen sharply.

This is in direct contrast to other cohorts I track, like MSTR investors, who (despite the negative price action) have actually been growing more convicted recently.

Interestingly, the lowest levels of conviction for this group happen precisely around the time that BIP-110 was officially proposed in October 2025.

So the takeaway IMO is not simply "BIP-110 folks are not confident they will succeed".

Conviction is related to the stories we tell ourselves.

We use stories as a way to make sense of the world, when stories crumble, so too does our conviction.

With that idea in mind, I believe the story driving this group came under pressure. This is evident in that rapid downturn in the amount of conviction they expressed throughout 2025.

Although their net conviction is slowly climbing back up from the lows, this group still remains much less confident than the broader Bitcoin ecosystem during a time where tensions and arguments are heating up.

I'm going to keep watching this closely. But regardless of what happens over the coming weeks, this data shows that Bitcoin debates are never purely technical. 

Even when the conversation focuses on code, policy, or protocol details, there are emotional and human dynamics lurking beneath the surface that are impossible to escape from.

BREAKING: Interest expense on US public debt as a % of GDP is up to ~3.2%, the highest since at least the 1970s.

This figure has nearly TRIPLED over the last 5 years.

Over the same period, national defense spending as a % of GDP has fallen to ~3.0%, the lowest since the early 2000s.

As a result, interest expense has exceeded national defense spending for 3 consecutive years, the longest streak in at least 46 years.

Meanwhile, nominal interest payments have risen +$711 billion since 2020, or +140%, to a record annualized rate of $1.22 trillion.

Over the same period, defense spending has increased +$237 billion, or +35%, to a record annualized rate of $923 billion.

America's debt burden is in uncharted territory.

China is now dominating the global auto market:

China's vehicle exports jumped +68.7% YoY in May, to ~930,000.

This is almost +1,100% above levels seen in May 2019.

This comes as new EV exports surged +112.6% YoY, to 424,000, accounting for ~46% of the total.

As a result, China exported a record 8.6 million vehicles in the 12 months ending May.

By comparison, Japan exported just 4.2 million, or -51% fewer, during the same period.

To put this into perspective, China exported just 1.0 million vehicles in 2019, while Japan exported 4.8 million, or +380% more.

China is now the undisputed leader of the global car market.

The more intensely we long for things, the more they tend to elude us. Most of us have experienced this at some point in our lives (I certainly have).

The beautiful woman who senses desperation rejects you. The fisherman who doesn't care whether he catches anything always brings in the most fish.

Would it surprise you if I said that the exact same dynamic exists in relationship to the Bitcoin price?

Would it surprise you if I said that this seemingly "woo-woo" idea was quantifiable?

It sure as hell surprised me.

See there are small cues that exist embedded inside the words we use to communicate with one another. Little language tells that uncover underlying emotions and give us cues to what individuals are feeling.

Most of the time this happens subconsciously... but it does happen, and you can measure it based on the words people choose over time.

I've done this across the Bitcoin ecosystem with nearly 30 different emotional profiles, but the most interesting one IMO is "desire".

I didn't go into this little experiment with any expectations.

I just wanted to observe which emotions the crowd was feeling, and whether any of them might be correlated to the Bitcoin price in interesting ways.

Then I saw this chart.

High desire (gold) in bull markets often directly preceded large sell offs.

Low levels of desire (blue) in bear markets often marked fantastic buying opportunities.

There are potential logical reasons for this (my most recent newsletter goes deep into this) but I can't help but to keep thinking about some of these phrases that spiritual teachers and philosophers have echoed for millennia.

"To come to possess all, desire to possess nothing."

"One who gives up material desires and ego attains perfect peace."

"Freedom is secured not by the fulfilling of men's desires, but by the removal of desire."

I've seen this advice play out in my own life as I've grown to have more faith as I move through life and embrace the weirdness of my own life journey, but I'd never expected to see it show up in data like this. 

But maybe I should have?

Language and story are a much more profound technology than most people realize. There is a lot more hidden beneath the surface in each of us.

Anyways... I'll let you develop your own opinions about what this all means.

But I personally find the fact that Bitcoiners are using some of the lowest levels of "desiring" language on record to be quite bullish for the orange coin. 

Hope this hits a little different than the other Bitcoin price charts you're seeing on the timeline today.

Cheers ✌️
